correctness.rationale: For \(x=a e_0+b e_1+c e_2\), direct multiplication gives the exact three quadratic equations in RESULT.md. Their sum forces augmentation \(s\) to satisfy \(s^2=s\). Pairwise differences factor as \((a-b)(s-1-3c)\), \((b-c)(s-1-3a)\), and \((c-a)(s-1-3b)\). These factorizations give the eight solutions when \(3\) is invertible and reduce the characteristic-three augmentation-one locus to \((a-b)^2=a+b\), which has the stated one-parameter solution. The standalone checker exactly enumerates finite test fields, including \(\mathbb F_9\), and ends with CHECK_OK. No finite enumeration is used as a proof of the arbitrary-field theorem.

value.rationale: The result identifies the exact coefficient-field boundary for the smallest latin dihedral quandle, a canonical test object in the current idempotent-conjecture literature. It turns a previously exhibited isolated field-valued idempotent into a complete classification and shows a qualitative modular degeneration: a finite eight-point set becomes an affine line exactly in characteristic \(3\). This is a natural structural boundary rather than an arbitrary finite census, and it calibrates how integral/Fourier rigidity behaves under scalar extension.
